acceptanceClaims: peer A completed its physical one-shot service before valid Actor authority was admitted, yet the actor-authorized S6 profile retained peer-A current world truth and performed no topology replacement
nonexistent authority, wrong zone, and wrong capability requests were rejected before physical mutation
the valid Actor effect request was bound to exact RangeAuthority, zone, capability, request, admission, and effect identities
exact in-process replay of Security admission and backend request converged without duplicate request events
the backend receipt retained worldEffectVerified=false while Host Linux netlink independently established peer-A removal and peer-B addition
the maintained Windows Guest and external packet sensor both observed peer-A and peer-B challenge flows and residual closure was clean
the same implementation passed a separate physical regression of the original backend-owned S6 profile
limitations: one typed peer-replacement effect is accepted; this is not a generic Range action, RBAC, or policy framework
the acceptance runner deterministically generated the Actor request rather than a model selecting it strategically
RangeSession effect admission and replay state remain process-local and are not resumable after controller replacement
exactly-once physical effect semantics across process death are not proved
RangeEvent causalParents remain descriptive rather than a validated causal graph
the accepted Range remains isolated and structurally unrouted with no external target authority

setupFalsifier.failure: the first C1 state root was mode 0700, preventing the qemu-owned swtpm process from traversing the experiment root before RangeSession startup
